data.title: Oil markets are on edge ahead of the weekend, as midterm elections near and fresh U.S. strikes on Iran are predicted
data.description:
By Isabel Wang and Myra P. Saefong

Global oil prices are closing in on their highest levels since the Iran war began

Oil has climbed back to an Iran-war high and may soon go higher, if the U.S. and Israel strike Iran after their respective voters go to the polls in the coming days.

Eight months into the Iran war, the global energy crisis is showing no signs of easing. Instead, oil prices were surging again, hurtling toward their highest levels since the conflict began in February and stoking fears that the world is heading toward an even more punishing energy crunch.

"Worries about oil back over $100 a barrel and the Iran conflict flaring up again are top of mind heading into the weekend," said Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group.

Global Brent crude for December delivery (BRN00) (BRNZ26) jumped 3.4% to $111.44 a barrel Friday afternoon, putting the benchmark within striking distance of its wartime settlement high of $118.35, reached in late March. West Texas Intermediate crude for December delivery (CL.1) (CLZ26) also climbed 3.5% to $103.09 a barrel. It settled as high as $112.95 in April, its highest level since the Iran war began, according to FactSet data.

The recent uptick in oil prices comes as the Iran-backed Houthis conducted further drone strikes Wednesday on Saudi airports and the Saudi Aramco Shaybah oil field, attacks that earlier this week led the U.S. to order embassy staff in Riyadh to leave the country. Trump has warned that the U.S. could attack Iran anew after the Nov. 3 midterm elections, and both the U.S. and Israel have been preparing options for strikes after voters go to the polls. Israel holds its elections on Tuesday.

Another risk for energy markets: Iran said that if U.S. and Israeli bombings resume, Tehran will respond with strikes on pipelines and airports in oil-rich Persian Gulf countries, according to Wall Street Journal reporting.

"Iran is agitating to keep oil prices high and push down American popular support for the Trump administration and the war," said Matt Gertken, chief geopolitical and U.S. political strategist at BCA Research. "But after the election President Trump will intensify strikes to try to coerce Iran's leaders into a ceasefire."

Trump on Thursday hinted at fresh action against Iran during a speech in Iowa.

"We're going to have Iran finished very soon," he said in Sioux City. "One way or the other, it's going to be done very soon, and your gasoline prices and your oil is going to come tumbling down."

Anna Kelly, a White House spokeswoman, said in an emailed response to MarketWatch on Friday that the U.S. will not be attacking Iran "at any time" prior to the midterm elections.

"As President Trump stated, Iran is in very bad condition, both economically and militarily, and the blockade will remain in full force and effect, with oil flowing in record numbers of barrels through the Hormuz Strait," she said.

But oil's climb back toward its wartime highs is more than a geopolitical story. It's the clearest sign yet of how exposed Trump and the Republicans are to the one issue they can't spin: the price at the pump. The national average price for a gallon of regular gasoline is $4.29, according to AAA. That's up from less than $3 a gallon before the war.

It's a test not just for a stock market already juggling earnings, an upcoming interest-rate decision from the Federal Reserve and mounting worries about debt related to the artificial-intelligence build-out, but also for Trump and his party, who have staked so much on the economy ahead of a crucial moment that could shape the direction of the president's final two years in office.

Beyond a possible fresh U.S. attack on Iran, the post-midterm outlook is cloudy. Democrats appear poised to take control of at least one chamber of Congress and have pledged to try to wind down the Iran war. But they're unlikely to win enough seats to override a Trump veto of a bill that would restrict military operations, as a longtime national security expert wrote in a CNN analysis.

Trump, for his part, has taken steps to ease the pressure on energy markets, including temporarily allowing Russia to supply diesel to U.S. and other markets and announcing plans to use Defense Production Act funding to expand oil production and refining.

That move opens up money for oil projects, but it takes years to build a refinery. So really, "this is a policy for the 2030 diesel market," Giacomo Prandelli, a commodity analyst and geopolitical strategist and the writer of a newsletter called Merchant's News, said on X. Voters will soon go to the polls, and they "pay today's prices."

"The oil market isn't pricing availability alone. It's pricing reliability," said Angie Gildea, global head of oil and gas at KPMG, in comments to MarketWatch. "Even when barrels are flowing, concerns about energy infrastructure and shipping routes can keep a risk premium in prices."

With no end to the Iran conflict in sight, market analysts see oil prices staying elevated even in the aftermath of the midterms.

Brent crude could remain in the range of $110 to $120 a barrel for a while, further increasing inflation risks, said Fawad Razaqzada, global macroeconomic market analyst at StoneX Trading and Forex.com. "That in turn could be bad news for all sorts of risk assets," he told MarketWatch on Friday.

Gertken at BCA Research said consumers can handle oil prices that average $105 a barrel over the coming months, but not an increase to $160. However, should oil reach $160 a barrel, the Trump administration might try "toppling the Iranian regime," he said. "So Iran will probably not drive prices that high."

He expects to see U.S. strikes intensifying in the coming months, and then both the U.S. and Iran opting for negotiations due to a "lack of economic and political capabilities to support a longer war."

Both the U.S. and global oil benchmarks have risen for three consecutive weeks and on Friday were on pace for their biggest three-week advance since early September, according to FactSet data.

Robert Schroeder and Joy Wiltermuth contributed.

-Isabel Wang -Myra P. Saefong

data.title: Kidney Patients Back Bipartisan Bill to Expand Disability Employment
data.description:
Kidney Patients Back Bipartisan Bill to Expand Disability Employment

Kidney Patients Back Bipartisan Bill to Expand Disability Employment

PR Newswire

WASHINGTON, Oct. 23, 2026

U.S. Representatives Hoyer and Sessions Lead AbilityOne Modernization Bill

Kidney Disease and Jobs are Focus of National Disability Employment Month

WASHINGTON, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The American Association of Kidney Patients (AAKP), the nation's oldest and largest independent kidney patient advocacy organization, today announced plans to accelerate national grassroots patient advocacy in support of bipartisan legislation that will modernize the federal AbilityOne program. The American Procurement Improvement Act (APIA), H.R. 10443, is championed by U.S. Representatives Pete Sessions (R-TX) and Steny Hoyer (D-MD). AAKP defines kidney disease as both an American healthcare and workforce issue and fights to expand career opportunities and job protections for all Americans impacted by kidney disease, disabilities, and chronic diseases.

The AbilityOne program creates private sector employment opportunities for over 41,000 Americans with severe vision and other disabilities, including nearly 3,000 American Veterans. In FY 2025, the program generated nearly 48 million direct labor hours, an 8 percent increase and a significant measure of disability employment growth, with workers working and working more hours. AbilityOne delivered more than $4.7 billion in products and services to the Federal government in FY 2025 and drew discouraged workers into the U.S. labor force while supporting greater workforce participation, increasing economic independence, and self-sufficiency. The AbilityOne mission taps the underutilized workforce of people with significant disabilities to deliver high-quality, mission-essential products and services to federal agencies, including the U.S. Department of Defense and the U.S. Department of Homeland Security.

The APIA legislation removes outdated statutory barriers to hiring, retention, advancement, and movement into careers of choice, including emerging fields and new lines of business. It also modernizes federal procurement by aligning AbilityOne with contemporary procurement practices and streamlines procurement processes so the program can respond faster to emerging federal agency priorities. The APIA legislation protects taxpayer interests, strengthens program accountability and stewardship by preserving oversight, transparency, and worker protections while modernizing AbilityOne Commission authorities. The legislation is seen as an opportunity to improve federal procurement and strengthen the federal government's domestic supplier base.

Over 36 million Americans live with kidney disease, over 600,000 are on dialysis, and nearly 100,000 are awaiting a kidney transplant. Further, interrelated cardiovascular, kidney, and metabolic diseases have impacted more than 25% of the adult population and are a leading cause of death. More broadly, the American Heart Association estimates that 90% of U.S. adults, or about 240 million people, have some degree of interconnected cardiovascular, kidney, or metabolic health conditions. For kidney patients dependent upon status-quo, in-center hemodialysis, burdensome thrice-weekly dialysis sessions force many patients, against their own choosing, into unemployment, disability, and dependency. AAKP believes dialysis-related unemployment, and the associated costs borne by families and taxpayers, is one of the media's least-reported stories in legacy kidney care. AAKP's policy agenda focuses on transplant readiness, more opportunities for organ transplants, more flexible, patient-centered home dialysis solutions, and stronger job protections for both kidney patients and living organ donors.

AAKP President Edward V. Hickey, III, a chronic kidney disease patient, stated, "AAKP strongly endorses the American Procurement Improvement Act (APIA) and expresses our deepest gratitude to Representatives Steny Hoyer and Peter Sessions for their bipartisan leadership and commitment to Americans managing disabilities and their efforts to secure meaningful employment opportunities with solid wages. People impacted by disability and chronic diseases face tremendous hurdles to continued employment and return to the workforce - especially America's proud Veterans. This legislation reflects consensus language among stakeholders, including advocates, employers, and organized labor, and sends a very positive message, amid national economic concerns, that the voices and needs of disabled Americans and their families are heard and not forgotten by the U.S. Congress. We encourage Congress to step up and pass this legislation before the close of the year." Hickey is a U.S. Marine Corps Veteran, a former senior congressional aide, and has served in appointed roles in two presidential administrations, including the U.S. Department of Commerce (DOC) and the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM). At OPM, he was heavily involved in policy issues related to federal Veterans preference in civil service hiring and expanded federal job opportunities. He currently serves on the American Board of Internal Medicine's (ABIM) Nephrology Specialty Board and as the Chair of the AAKP Veterans Health Initiative, the largest kidney health outreach program outside of the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs.

October is National Disability Employment Month, and AAKP and its allies remind elected and appointed government leaders to address health and employment concerns that impact patients, families, and communities. Through multiple partnerships, AAKP leads the kidney community in providing kidney patients and transplant recipients, including Veterans, access to virtual job fairs and employment skills training opportunities. AAKP is currently sponsoring virtual job fairs, in partnership with CareerEco, on January 13, 2027, and May 18, 2027, that will service Veterans and military families. AAKP's past collaborations have included webinars with Idealist and virtual disability and Veteran hiring fairs with Bender Consulting.

AAKP Vice President and Chair of Policy and Global Affairs Paul T. Conway, a 49-year kidney patient and 29-year transplant recipient, stated, "The AbilityOne program has supported private sector employment for people managing disabilities and chronic diseases for nearly ninety years and reflects the exceptional American values of self-reliance and independence. Representatives Steny Hoyer and Pete Sessions have consistently shown respect for the creativity, talents, and skills of disabled citizens and have dedicated their public careers to expanding job opportunities in the workforce and across the federal supply chain. The American Procurement Improvement Act increases accountability for taxpayer funds and will result in more well-paying jobs for Americans whose desire and capacity to work and contribute are underappreciated." Conway is a former Chief of Staff for both the U.S. Department of Labor and the U.S. Office of Personnel Management and a former Deputy Secretary for Health and Human Resources for the Commonwealth of Virginia. He has overseen multiple federal and state disability employment, workforce training, and health service programs throughout his public career. He is the past Chair of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's Patient Engagement Advisory Committee (PEAC) and serves on the Observational Study Monitoring Board of the Kidney Precision Medicine Program (KPMP) administered by the National Institutes of Health, National Institute of Diabetes, Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIH/NIDDK).

To advance the APIA, AAKP is working with former U.S. Representative Tony Coelho, Chair of the Partnership to Improve Patient Care as well as the Alliance for Expanding America's Workforce. Along with AAKP, APIA is endorsed by over 60 national patient and disability organizations, labor unions and employers including the American Association of People with Disabilities, SEIU, Bender Consulting, National Council of SourceAmerica Employers, CEO Commission for Disability Employment, the Arc of the United States, National Organization on Disability, National Down Syndrome Society, National Disability Rights Network, National Federation of the Blind, Melwood Inc., WORK Inc., ORC Industries, Employment Source, Opportunity Center, Inc., PARC, ACHIEVE Human Services, Inc., Human Technologies, InspiriTec, PORTCO Inc, PRIDE Industries, Phoenix, Pueblo Diversified Industries, and the Association of People Supporting EmploymentFirst (APSE).

AAKP, alongside a broad and diverse coalition of patient organizations, transplant experts, and Congressional allies, is also working to secure passage of the Living Donor Protection Act (LDPA), S. 1552/H.R. 4582 and H.R. 4583, in 2026. The bipartisan bill protects living organ donors from job and insurance discrimination based solely on their decision to donate a kidney to save another life, barriers cited most often by potential organ donors. The bipartisan legislation is led by Senator Tom Cotton (R-AK) and Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY). It was voted out of the Senate HELP Committee on February 26, 2026, with full bipartisan support, the endorsement of AAKP, the larger kidney community, and the American Council of Life Insurance (ACLI).

In 2018, with bipartisan support from Congress and the Trump Administration, AAKP and transplant professionals worked with the U.S. Department of Labor's (DOL) legal team and the DOL Wage and Hour Division to have DOL issue Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) protections for living organ donors, based on the original intent of the FMLA's Congressional co-sponsors (click here to read the letter and click here to watch the video). Congressional passage of the LDPA in 2026 will codify the DOL's 2018 FMLA job protections and prohibit insurers from discriminating against living donors. Increased living organ donation, improved transplant readiness among kidney patients, and greater opportunities for transplantation have been national goals for decades and were reinforced in 2019 through the Executive Order on Advancing American Kidney Health.

Follow AAKP on social media at @kidneypatient on Facebook, @kidneypatients on X, and @kidneypatients on Instagram, and visit https://aakp.org/ for more information. AAKP patient advocates advance bipartisan kidney policy including: passage of the bipartisan law modernizing the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN) (2023); lifetime transplant drug coverage for kidney patients (2020); the historic Executive Order on Advancing American Kidney Health signed by President Donald Trump (2019); job protections for living organ donors under the Family Medical Leave Act (FMLA) via the U.S. Department of Labor (2018); and Congressional approval of HIV positive organ transplants for HIV positive patients (2013).

data.title: Novo's Awiqli® receives FDA approval as the first and only once-weekly insulin for children 10 years of age and older with type 2 diabetes
data.description:
Novo's Awiqli® receives FDA approval as the first and only once-weekly insulin for children 10 years of age and older with type 2 diabetes

Novo's Awiqli® receives FDA approval as the first and only once-weekly insulin for children 10 years of age and older with type 2 diabetes

PR Newswire

PLAINSBORO, N.J., Oct. 23, 2026
  • Awiqli® offers children 10 years and older a once-weekly basal insulin alternative, reducing basal injection frequency from seven times per week to one1
  • As type 2 diabetes incidence rates among youth continue to rise,² Awiqli® may help reduce administration barriers associated with daily basal insulin injections and provide families access to more individualized care
  • This approval of Awiqli® reflects Novo's ongoing efforts to advance healthcare innovation and strengthen support for people living with diabetes and their caregivers

PLAINSBORO, N.J., Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Novo Nordisk today announced that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Awiqli® (insulin icodec-abae) injection 700 units/mL, the first once-weekly, long-acting basal insulin, as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control (blood sugar) in children 10 years of age and older with type 2 diabetes.1 This approval offers a once-weekly basal insulin treatment option, which reduces the frequency of weekly basal injections from seven to one per week.1

"Individuals with type 2 diabetes and their families seek treatment options that may allow for more individualized care. Awiqli® reduces basal insulin injections from seven to one per week, which may help patients find a basal insulin routine that feels more manageable," said Michael Radin, MD, executive medical director at Novo. "It is important to continue to discover advanced treatments for the populations that need them today."

Type 2 diabetes in children and adolescents is a growing public health challenge, as more young people are being diagnosed each year with this chronic disease that requires ongoing care and caregiver support.3 According to a modeling study, it's anticipated that the number of people ≤19 years old with type 2 diabetes is estimated to reach nearly 84,000 by 2050.4 Healthy nutrition, physical activity, and family support are important aspects of care for type 2 diabetes.2 However, for some young people, these measures may not be enough, potentially leading to complications related to this disease.5 Novo's approach to pediatric care emphasizes a comprehensive model of support – promoting healthy nutrition, regular physical activity, and diabetes education, alongside proven, age-appropriate treatment options for children and adolescents living with type 2 diabetes.2 

This approval is supported by evidence from adequate and well-controlled studies in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and a single-dose pharmacokinetic study completed in pediatric patients that evaluated the pharmacokinetic properties of once-weekly Awiqli® injection in pediatric patients (10 to <18 years of age) with type 2 diabetes.6 These results support the use of Awiqli® in pediatric patients (at least 10 years of age and older), along with the efficacy and safety demonstrated in the pivotal ONWARDS clinical trial program.6,9 Common side effects of Awiqli® may include: hypoglycemia (low blood sugar), serious allergic reactions (whole body reactions), reactions at the injection site, skin thickening or pits at the injection site (lipodystrophy), itching, rash, swelling of your hands and feet, and weight gain.1

"Children with type 2 diabetes face an aggressive disease trajectory and achieving sustained glycemic control in children with type 2 diabetes remains a major challenge. We need treatments that are not only effective but options that work for different patient routines. Having alternative options available for basal insulin therapy allows patients to find a treatment that works best for them and their lifestyle and helps them manage their type 2 diabetes. For more than 20 years daily basal insulin injections have been a main form of treatment in pediatric diabetes care, but children living with type 2 diabetes may face challenges staying on a daily treatment routine," said Eda Cengiz, MD, MHS Professor of Pediatrics at the University of California, San Francisco. "Having an FDA-approved, once-weekly basal insulin injection available could provide new alternatives for pediatric clinical care. Offering a once-weekly basal insulin may help reduce administration barriers associated with daily insulin injections and provide clinicians and families access to more individualized care."

Awiqli® is available at more than 70,000 pharmacies nationwide. More information can be found at www.awiqli.com.

Please see below for Important Safety Information and please click here for the full Prescribing Information.

About Awiqli®
Awiqli® (insulin icodec-abae) injection 700 units/mL is a prescription medicine and is the first and only FDA-approved once-weekly basal insulin indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults and children with type 2 diabetes.1 Awiqli® is designed as an alternative to daily basal insulin and its FDA approval is supported by the ONWARDS clinical program, which evaluated its efficacy and safety across insulin-naive patients and previously treated with insulin patient populations living with type 2 diabetes. This approval is supported by evidence from adequate and well-controlled studies in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and a single-dose pharmacokinetic study completed in pediatric patients that evaluated the pharmacokinetic properties of once-weekly Awiqli® injection in pediatric patients (10 to <18 years of age) with type 2 diabetes.6 These results support the use of Awiqli® in pediatric patients (at least 10 years and older), along with the efficacy and safety demonstrated in the pivotal ONWARDS clinical trial program.6-10 Awiqli® is administered once-weekly on the same day each week using the Awiqli® FlexTouch® pen.1 Awiqli® is approved in the US, EU, and 18 additional countries, with market-specific indications for diabetes.

What is Awiqli?

  • Prescription Awiqli® (insulin icodec-abae) injection 700 units/mL is a long-acting insulin (U-700) that is used to control high blood sugar in adults and children who are 10 years of age and older with type 2 diabetes mellitus
  • It is not known if Awiqli® is safe and effective in children less than 10 years of age
  • Awiqli® is available in 1 concentration: U-700

Important Safety Information

Do not share your Awiqli® FlexTouch® pen or needles with other people, even if the needle has been changed. You may give other people a serious infection, or get a serious infection from them.

Make sure you use the right type and dose of insulin. Always check the label on your insulin pen before each injection to avoid mix-ups with Awiqli® and other insulin products or injectable medicines used to treat diabetes. If you use another injectable medicine to treat your diabetes, pay close attention to how you select your Awiqli® dosage. The dosage of Awiqli® is different from other injectable medicines used to treat diabetes.

Always make sure that you select the correct dosage of your Awiqli® FlexTouch® pen as prescribed by your healthcare provider, to avoid dosing errors and accidental overdose. People who are blind or have vision problems should not use this pen without help from a person trained to use the pen.

Do not dial the maximum single dosage (700 units) of your Awiqli® FlexTouch® pen, unless prescribed by your healthcare provider.

Do not use a syringe to withdraw Awiqli® from your pen.

Talk to your healthcare provider if you have any questions about how to correctly dose Awiqli® FlexTouch®.

Who should not take Awiqli®?

Do not take Awiqli® if you:

  • are having an episode of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia)
  • have an allergy to Awiqli® or any of the ingredients in Awiqli®. See the full Patient Information for a complete listing of ingredients in Awiqli® 

Before taking Awiqli®, tell your healthcare provider about all your medical conditions, including if you:

  • have liver or kidney problems
  • take other medicines, especially ones called TZDs (thiazolidinediones)
  • have heart failure or other heart problems. If you have heart failure, it may get worse while you take TZDs with Awiqli®
  • are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or are breastfeeding
  • are taking new prescription or over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements

Talk to your health care provider about low blood sugar and how to manage it.

How should I take Awiqli® FlexTouch®?

  • Read the Instructions for Use that come with your Awiqli® FlexTouch® pen
  • Your healthcare provider should show you how to use Awiqli® FlexTouch® pen before you use it for the first time
  • Take Awiqli® exactly as your healthcare provider tells you to. Do not do any conversion of your dose. The dose counter always shows the selected dose in units. Awiqli® FlexTouch® pens are made to deliver your insulin dose in units
  • Know the type and strength of insulin you take. Do not change the type of insulin you take unless your health care provider tells you to. The amount of insulin and best time for you to take your insulin may need to change if you take different types of insulin
  • Inject Awiqli® FlexTouch® 1 time each week on any day of the week on the same day each week
  • If you need to change the day of the week, you may do so if your last dose has been at least 4 days
  • If you have missed your dose, take your missed dose as soon as possible as long as it has been 4 days or less. Then continue the 1 time each week schedule 1 week from the day your missed dose was taken
  • If more than 4 days have passed, skip the missed dose and take your next Awiqli® dose on your regularly scheduled day.
  • Check your blood sugar levels. Ask your health care provider what your blood sugar levels should be and when you should check them
  • Never inject Awiqli® FlexTouch® into a vein or muscle or use Awiqli® in an infusion pump
  • Never use a syringe to remove Awiqli® from the FlexTouch® pen
  • Do not dilute or mix Awiqli® with any other insulin or solution
  • Awiqli® FlexTouch® can be injected under the skin (subcutaneously) of your upper legs (thighs), upper arms, or stomach area (abdomen)
  • Change (rotate) your injection sites within the area you choose with each dose to reduce your risk of getting lipodystrophy (pits in skin or thickened skin) and localized cutaneous amyloidosis (skin with lumps) at the injection sites.
    • Do not use the exact same spot for each injection
    • Do not inject where the skin has pits, is thickened, or has lumps
    • Do not inject where the skin is tender, bruised, scaly or hard, or into scars or damaged skin
  • Keep Awiqli and all medicines out of the reach of children.

What should I avoid while taking Awiqli®?

  • Do not drive or operate heavy machinery, until you know how Awiqli® affects you
  • Do not drink alcohol or use prescription or over-the-counter medicines that contain alcohol

What are the possible side effects of Awiqli®?

Awiqli® may cause serious side effects that can be life-threatening, including:

  • Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia). Signs and symptoms that may indicate low blood sugar include: dizziness or light-headedness, sweating, confusion, fast heartbeat, blurred vision, slurred speech, shakiness, anxiety, irritability, mood changes, hunger and headache
  • Severe allergic reactions (whole body reaction). Stop using Awiqli and get medical help right away, if you have any of these signs or symptoms of a severe allergic reaction: a rash over your whole body, trouble breathing, a fast heartbeat or sweating
  • Low potassium in your blood (hypokalemia)
  • Heart failure in some people if taken with thiazolidinediones (TZDs). This can happen even if you have never had heart failure or heart problems. If you already have heart failure, it may get worse while you take TZDs with Awiqli®. Tell your health care provider if you have any new or worse symptoms of heart failure including shortness of breath, tiredness, swelling of your ankles or feet, and sudden weight gain

Your insulin dose may need to change because of change in level of physical activity or exercise, increased stress, change in diet, weight gain or loss, or illness

Common side effects may include: hypoglycemia, serious allergic reactions (whole body reactions), reactions at the injection site, skin thickening or pits at the injection site (lipodystrophy), itching, rash, swelling of your hands and feet, and weight gain

Get emergency medical help if you have trouble breathing, shortness of breath, fast heartbeat, swelling of your face, tongue, or throat, sweating, extreme drowsiness, dizziness, or confusion

These are not all the possible side effects of Awiqli®. Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects. You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

Please click here for the full Prescribing Information.

data.title: 1845 Distilling Co. Nominated Finalist for "Best Wheated Bourbon" at 2026 San Francisco World Spirits Competition
data.description:
1845 Distilling Co. Nominated Finalist for "Best Wheated Bourbon" at 2026 San Francisco World Spirits Competition

1845 Distilling Co. Nominated Finalist for "Best Wheated Bourbon" at 2026 San Francisco World Spirits Competition

PR Newswire

LOWRY CROSSING, Texas, Oct. 23, 2026

99-point Bourbon earns the Family-Owned Texas Distillery its Third "Best of Class Finalist" recognition in Four Competitions

LOWRY CROSSING, Texas, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- 1845 Distilling Co.'s Preemption Texas Wheated Bottled in Bond Bourbon has been named as one of four Finalists for Best Wheated Bourbon at the 2026 San Francisco World Spirits Competition. Each of the Four Finalists earned 99 Points.

The Five Year Old, 100 Proof Bourbon received one of three Double Gold Medals awarded to 1845 Distilling Co. in the 2026 Competition, which is the largest and most influential blind tasting event in the world. Their Preemption Reverence Texas Straight Cask Strength Bourbon and Preemption Double Oak Bourbon each received scores of 96.

This marks 1845's Third "Best of Class" Finalist recognition across the last four competitions, with three different expressions earning a place among the finalists:

  • 2023 — Bourbon: Preemption Texas Straight Bourbon, 100 proof, aged three years, earning 96 points. This was the first spirit released by the Company.
  • 2025 — Craft Distiller Whiskey: Texian No. 1 Texas Straight Whiskey, earning 97 points.
  • 2026 — Wheated Bourbon: Preemption Texas Wheated Bottled In Bond Bourbon, aged five years, earning 99 points.

For the Family-owned distillery, the recognition reflects a sustained commitment to Texas grain and Grain-to-Glass production. 1845 exclusively uses grain grown in Texas, connecting the finished spirit to the farmers and agricultural heritage of Texas.

"Being named a finalist once is an honor. Earning that recognition three times, with three different whiskeys, is especially meaningful to our Family," said Bob Petitt, Founder of 1845 Distilling Co. "Our connection to Texas spans eight generations. We believe deeply in Texas grains and in the spirits we make from it. To see our five year old wheated bourbon standing among four finalists, each with 99 points, is a proud moment for our Family and for the Texas farmers whose grain makes it possible."

The "Bottled in Bond" designation reflects defined production and aging standards: Whiskey produced by one distiller, during one distilling season, aged at least four years in a federally bonded warehouse, and bottled at 100 proof. The 1845 Finalist expression is aged five years.

The 2026 "Best in Class" Results will be announced November 8th at the competition's gala to be held in San Francisco.

About 1845 Distilling Co.

1845 Distilling Co. is a Family-owned and operated craft distillery in Lowry Crossing, Texas, minutes from Downtown McKinney, and in the Heart of Collin County. With a Grain-to-Glass approach using grain grown entirely in Texas, 1845 produces bourbon and whiskey rooted in Texas agriculture, family craftsmanship, and patient barrel ageing.

data.title: PATRICK TA BEAUTY APPOINTS ANGELA SIMPSON AS CHIEF MARKETING OFFICER AND CAROLYNE RAPP AS VICE PRESIDENT OF CREATIVE
data.description:
PATRICK TA BEAUTY APPOINTS ANGELA SIMPSON AS CHIEF MARKETING OFFICER AND CAROLYNE RAPP AS VICE PRESIDENT OF CREATIVE

PATRICK TA BEAUTY APPOINTS ANGELA SIMPSON AS CHIEF MARKETING OFFICER AND CAROLYNE RAPP AS VICE PRESIDENT OF CREATIVE

PR Newswire

LOS ANGELES, Oct. 23, 2026

New Executive Hires Strengthen Leadership Team as Patrick Ta Beauty Enters Its Next Chapter

LOS ANGELES, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Patrick Ta Beauty today announced the appointments of Angela Simpson as Chief Marketing Officer and Carolyne Rapp as Vice President of Creative, effective immediately. Since launching in 2019 by co-founders Patrick Ta, Rima Minasyan and Avo Minasyan, Patrick Ta Beauty has established itself as a leader in prestige makeup through a deeply rooted commitment to artistry, translating Patrick's signature techniques and approach to modern glamour into products designed for everyone. Today, the brand continues to build on its momentum across product innovation, artistry and creative storytelling, with the appointments further strengthening its leadership team.

"When I think about the future of Patrick Ta Beauty, I think about continuing to evolve our brand expression while staying true to what got us here," shares co-founder, Patrick Ta. "I've always wanted Patrick Ta Beauty to be more than a beauty brand. As a creative, I think about the visual world we're building, the experiences we're creating and how we can connect artistry to culture. That's what makes bringing Angela and Carolyne into this next chapter so exciting for me. Angela understands how to build the heartbeat of a brand and create real brand love, and Carolynne has a creative point of view that I've always admired. I'm excited to partner with them and continue building the legacy of this brand alongside such inspiring women."

As Chief Marketing Officer, Simpson brings more than two decades of experience building global beauty brands across marketing, innovation and commercial growth – and in her new role, she will help shape Patrick Ta Beauty's continued growth and global marketing strategy. Most recently, she served as Chief Marketing Officer of Haus Labs by Lady Gaga, leading the company's global marketing organization and go-to-market strategy. Prior to Haus Labs, she spent nine years at NARS Cosmetics, where she most recently served as Senior Vice President of U.S. Marketing, helping grow the brand from the No. 13 to No. 7 prestige makeup brand in the U.S. and leading the launch of Light Reflecting Foundation, the No. 1 prestige makeup launch of 2022. Earlier in her career, Simpson held leadership roles at Sephora and L'Oréal Paris.

"We've come a long way since Patrick and I first set out to build this brand, and it's incredibly rewarding to see how Patrick Ta Beauty continues to grow and evolve," shares co-founder, Rima Minasyan. "Angela and Carolyne bring a depth of experience and valuable perspective, and we're thrilled to welcome them to our team as we enter this next chapter."

"Our focus has always been on building Patrick Ta Beauty with intention and creating the right foundation for long-term growth," adds Avo Minasyan, co-founder. "As the brand continues to scale, bringing in exceptional leaders like Angela and Carolyne will help us expand our capabilities, strengthen the business and build on the momentum we've created."

As Vice President of Creative, Rapp will lead Patrick Ta Beauty's creative direction, brand identity, campaigns and visual storytelling. She brings more than 15 years of experience building and evolving brands across beauty, fashion, retail and design, most recently serving as VP Creative Director at MERIT Beauty, where she led the brand's 360 creative vision across campaigns, social, copy, design, packaging, retail and collaborations. Earlier in her career, she held senior creative leadership roles at COS, Gap, Coach and Theory, including shaping COS's creative expression as the brand expanded internationally. She is also the founder of her own creative agency, Studio Rapp, where she has continued to consult across beauty, fashion and design.

The appointments come as Patrick Ta Beauty continues to expand its product portfolio and creative platforms, most recently introducing the Major Sculpt Shape & Shade Anywhere Artistry Sticks and Defining You, a campaign celebrating the individuality and artistry that spotlights seven makeup artists. The brand also continues to strengthen its position as a leader in blush, holding the No. 1 position in blush at Sephora in the U.S. in 2025, one of the largest categories in makeup. With Simpson leading marketing and Rapp overseeing creative, the pair will work closely with co-founders Patrick Ta, Rima Minasyan and Avo Minasyan, as well as Chief Executive Officer Kimberly Villatoro, to support the brand's continued evolution.

"Patrick Ta Beauty has experienced incredible momentum, and as we look toward the future, we're continuing to invest in the people and capabilities that will help us build thoughtfully and intentionally," said Villatoro. "Angela and Carolyne each bring a distinct expertise, but together they represent the combination of strategic thinking and creative vision we need for this next chapter. We're thrilled to welcome them to the team and excited about what we'll build together."

Simpson and Rapp's appointments reflect Patrick Ta Beauty's continued investment in the leadership needed to support its growth while building on the artistry and innovation that have defined the brand since its launch.

About Patrick Ta Beauty

In 2019, renowned celebrity makeup artist Patrick Ta, established product specialist, Rima Minasyan and seasoned entrepreneur, Avo Minasyan founded Patrick Ta Beauty. Taking inspiration from Patrick's signature glowing, sculpted makeup looks, the trio launched the brand with a mission to make red carpet artistry accessible to all – creating luxurious, easy-to-use formulas designed for both professionals and everyday beauty lovers. The brand is built on intentional innovation, focusing on products that elevate and simplify makeup application.

Patrick Ta Beauty is best known for its award-winning blushes as well as its glow-enhancing formulas, which emphasize the power of layering and dimensional color. Since launch, the brand has achieved top-tier rankings at Sephora, with a cult following among makeup artists, celebrities, and everyday beauty enthusiasts alike. Patrick Ta Beauty is shaping the future of modern luxury beauty, pushing boundaries with pro-inspired innovation that meets consumer-friendly functionality.

For more information, visit PatrickTa.com

What's Next for Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. Shareholders After 39.1% Stock Drop? Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP Explains Securities Fraud Class Action Lead Plaintiff Deadline

PR Newswire

LOS ANGELES, Oct. 23, 2026

Complaint alleges Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. misled investors between December 29, 2025 and June 29, 2026; investors may seek lead plaintiff role by November 2, 2026

LOS ANGELES, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP ("Glancy") announced today that the class action lawsuit covers investors who bought Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. ("Unicycive Therapeutics" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: UNCY) securities between December 29, 2025 and June 29, 2026. The Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. case, Patel v. Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc., was filed on September 3, 2026 in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California (Case No. 26-cv-09559).

Investors who suffered losses on Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. investments can submit their Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. loss information here before the November 2, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline.

Key dates in the Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. case

  • Class period: December 29, 2025 to June 29, 2026
  • Complaint filed: September 3, 2026
  • Lead plaintiff deadline: November 2, 2026

What happened?

On June 30, 2026, Unicycive Therapeutics disclosed that the FDA had issued a second Complete Response Letter regarding the Company's resubmitted New Drug Application for its kidney disease therapy, oxylanthanum carbonate, identifying the same third-party manufacturing deficiencies that were identified in the previous CRL issued in June 2025. The FDA had not yet inspected the third-party manufacturing facility as part of its review of the resubmission, and raised no concerns about the drug's clinical safety or efficacy.

On this news, Unicycive's stock price fell $3.01, or 39.1% (with some reports citing declines up to 46%), to close at $4.69 per share on June 30, 2026, thereby injuring investors.

What is the Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. lawsuit about?

The Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. securities lawsuit alleges that, between December 29, 2025 and June 29, 2026, defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts about Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc.'s business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, the complaint alleges defendants failed to disclose that: (1) the Company had not inspected its third-party manufacturing vendor's facility or otherwise audited the facility's compliance with current good manufacturing practices; (2) as a result, the Company lacked a reasonable basis to believe that the vendor had resolved the FDA's cited deficiencies; (3) there was an undisclosed risk that the FDA would require additional information about the vendor's facility's manufacturing practices; (4) as a result of the foregoing, the regulatory approval of OLC was reasonably likely to be delayed; and (5) as a result, defendants' positive statements about Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc.'s business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis.

"The complaint filed against Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. alleges that, among other things, the Company failed to disclose that the Company had not inspected its third-party manufacturing vendor's facility or otherwise audited the facility's compliance with current good manufacturing practices. For investors who bought during the class period, the November 2, 2026 deadline is the first major step in this case," said Charles H. Linehan, Partner at Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP.

What's the next step?

Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP is a leading national shareholder rights law firm, ready to assist Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. investors in potentially pursuing claims to recover their losses.

If you wish to serve as lead plaintiff in the Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. class action, you must move the Court no later than November 2, 2026. To learn more about your rights, visit the Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. case page, email shareholders@glancylaw.com, or call 310-201-9150 (toll-free: 888-773-9224).

You may retain counsel of your choice. If you bought Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. securities during the class period, you may take no action and remain an absent class member. No class has been certified yet in the Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. case.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is eligible? Investors who purchased or otherwise acquired Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. securities between December 29, 2025 and June 29, 2026 and suffered losses may be members of the proposed class in the Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. shareholder lawsuit. Any class member may ask the court to appoint them lead plaintiff by November 2, 2026.

What is a lead plaintiff? In the Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. class action, the lead plaintiff is the investor, or group of investors, that the court appoints to represent all class members and oversee the case. Under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act, courts generally presume the movant with the largest financial interest is the most adequate lead plaintiff.

Do I have to be lead plaintiff to recover? No. A Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. investor's ability to share in any future recovery does not depend on serving as lead plaintiff. Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. investors may take no action and remain absent class members.

What is the deadline? Motions to serve as lead plaintiff in the Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. class action must be filed by November 2, 2026.

Does it cost anything to contact Glancy or participate in this action? Glancy represents Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. investors on a contingency fee basis, which means investors pay no attorneys' fees unless there is a recovery. Any fees are subject to court approval and are paid from the recovery.

Can I choose my own lawyer? Yes. Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. investors may retain counsel of their choice.

Why work with Glancy on the Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. lawsuit? Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP is a premier law firm with decades of experience representing investors and consumers in securities litigation and other complex class action litigation. Contact Glancy about the Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. lawsuit. Prior results do not guarantee a similar outcome.

What Does Netcapital Inc.'s 28.62% Stock Drop Mean for Investors? The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith Outlines Securities Fraud Class Action Lead Plaintiff Deadline

PR Newswire

BENSALEM TOWNSHIP, Pa., Oct. 23, 2026

Suit alleges Netcapital Inc. failed to disclose key facts to investors from December 15, 2021 through September 3, 2026; lead plaintiff deadline is December 7, 2026

BENSALEM TOWNSHIP, Pa., Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith today reported that a securities class action lawsuit is pending against Netcapital Inc. ("Netcapital" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: NCPL) on behalf of investors who acquired its securities from December 15, 2021 through September 3, 2026. The Netcapital Inc. case, Chance v. Netcapital Inc. et al., was filed on October 8, 2026 in the U.S. District Court District of Massachusetts (Case No. 1:26-cv-14584).

Investors with losses on Netcapital Inc. securities can contact the Law Offices of Howard G. Smith about the Netcapital Inc. lawsuit before the December 7, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline.

Key deadlines and dates for Netcapital Inc. investors

  • Lead plaintiff deadline: December 7, 2026
  • Class period: December 15, 2021 through September 3, 2026
  • Complaint filed: October 8, 2026

What happened?

On August 10, 2026, the SEC filed a complaint against Netcapital and certain senior executives alleging, among other things, that Netcapital was involved in a fraudulent scheme to overstate the revenue of Netcapital. Specifically, from approximately October 2021 through January 2024, Netcapital improperly recorded nearly $14 million in revenue from sham consulting agreements which produced no real revenue for Netcapital. The recognition of this revenue inflated Netcapital's total revenue by approximately 345%. During this period, investors in Netcapital's public and private securities offerings invested over $25.6 million.

On this news, Netcapital stock fell $0.05 or 12.82%, to close at $0.35 on August 11, 2026, thereby injuring investors.

Then on August 17, 2026, the Netcapital disclosed that its independent registered public accounting firm, Fruci & Associates II, PLLC, had resigned.

On this news, Netcapital stock fell $0.09 or 28.62%, to close at $0.23 on August 18, 2026, thereby further injuring investors.

Finally on September 3, 2026, after market close, Netcapital disclosed that on Avi Liss had resigned as a member of the Board of Directors, and from all committees of the Board, including the Audit Committee, effective immediately. In his resignation letter, Liss stated that he was resigning "in light of the serious allegations recently asserted against the Company and certain current and former officers, directors, and other individuals" in the SEC Complaint.

On this news, Netcapital stock fell $0.05 per share, or 8.15%, to close at $0.58 per share on September 4, 2026. The following trading day, Netcapital stock fell a further $0.08 per share, or 13.15%, to close at $0.50 per share on September 8, 2026, thereby further injuring investors.

What is the Netcapital Inc. lawsuit about?

The Netcapital Inc. securities lawsuit alleges that, between December 15, 2021 and September 3, 2026, defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts about Netcapital Inc.'s business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, the complaint alleges defendants failed to disclose that: (1) Over the Class Period, Netcapital improperly recognized material revenues from what were, in reality, sham consulting agreements with entities controlled by Defendant John Fanning; (2) The consulting agreements were backdated and in some cases forged, and Netcapital Advisors provided little if any meaningful consulting services; (3) The Portfolio Company transactions were improperly undisclosed related-party transactions involving John Fanning; (4) Netcapital's certifications pursuant to the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 were false; and (5) as a result, defendants' positive statements about Netcapital Inc.'s business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis.

"The lawsuit against Netcapital Inc. alleges that, among other things, the Company failed to tell investors that Over the Class Period, Netcapital improperly recognized material revenues from what were, in reality, sham consulting agreements with entities controlled by Defendant John Fanning. Netcapital Inc. investors who bought during the class period may be able to pursue their losses, and the December 7, 2026 deadline is where that process begins," said Howard G. Smith of The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith.

Next steps for Netcapital Inc. investors

Netcapital Inc. investors who suffered losses may contact The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith to learn about pursuing their claims.

Lead plaintiff motions in the Netcapital Inc. class action are due to the Court by December 7, 2026. For more information, visit the firm's website, email howardsmith@howardsmithlaw.com, or call (215) 638-4847.

What is the deadline? Lead plaintiff motions in the Netcapital Inc. case are due by December 7, 2026.

Can I recover without being lead plaintiff? Yes, Netcapital Inc. investors may take no action and remain absent class members.

The firm prosecutes securities fraud, takeover, and derivative litigation against public companies and their officers, directors, and advisors in federal and state courts nationwide, and has helped clients recover hundreds of millions of dollars in losses. Infinity (Infinity Artificial Intelligence Institute) announces two key engineering hires: Aditya Om (left), a former senior software engineer at Meta Superintelligence Labs (MSL), joins Infinity as Staff Inference Optimization Engineer, and Elliot Arledge (right), whose CUDA and LLM coding courses have taught skills to more than two million people, joins as Member of Technical Staff.

“We’re hiring engineers to solve the greatest engineering challenges of our generation,” said Jeremy Nixon, founder and CEO of Infinity. “Aditya built inference stacks inside Meta Superintelligence Labs’ silicon program. Elliot taught millions of engineers how kernels actually work. Now they’re building automated AI research systems that create stronger AI models and inference frameworks than humans have ever built, so that every chip can run frontier AI."

Om and Arledge join Infinity at a pivotal time, as the company scales Ignition, its autonomous AI agent that compresses years of chip software development into days. Ignition’s coding-agent controller autonomously bootstraps every layer of a chip’s software stack.

Before joining Infinity, Om led development of the software stack for MSL’s in-house training and inference chips, built the collective communications software stack for Lightmatter’s Passage and where he published Envise in Nature, and worked as an IoT systems design engineer at Intel. He holds a Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science from the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor.

“Joining the team was a no-brainer,” said Om. “Inference has taken the world by storm. We have a pivotal shift in front of us, touching all areas of our lives, similar to the internet in the mid-90s. Infinity's mission of automating research in inference optimization so that the software layer is shaped to the custom hardware is the groundbreaking work I am passionate about.”

Arledge is a self-taught kernel engineer and CUDA expert who, at 22, has built coding courses that have taught millions of people to train LLMs from scratch & optimize CUDA kernels. “Chips are the core bottleneck of our time, and that’s exactly why I wanted to join Jeremy and Infinity,” said Arledge. “It takes a stubborn team of highly skilled, highly coordinated, ambitious people to pull this off.”

INFINITY.INC FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

What does Infinity do?
Infinity builds the software layer that makes any AI chip inference-ready. Its autonomous AI agent, Ignition, generates and optimizes inference software for new silicon in days, not years.

What is Ignition and how does it work?
Ignition is Infinity's AI research agent that autonomously writes, tests and optimizes the low-level compute kernels that determine how efficiently a chip runs AI models. It continuously improves through a real-world feedback loop, without human kernel engineers.

Why can't new AI chips compete with NVIDIA out of the box?
NVIDIA's CUDA ecosystem represents two decades of inference software development that rival chipmakers can't quickly replicate. Infinity closes that gap by automating the software development itself.

How fast can Infinity bring a new chip to production-ready AI inference?
In a published case study with d-Matrix, Infinity reached 92% of a new chip's theoretical peak performance within 10 hours of first hardware access, with three frontier models running end-to-end within 10 days.

Which chip companies is Infinity working with?
Infinity is currently in active partnership discussions with multiple major chip companies. Infinity's first live design partnership is with d-Matrix, whose Corsair chip runs production inference via the Infinity d-Matrix Cloud. Infinity also recently announced a collaboration with HP Inc. The two companies have been working together to use Infinity Autoresearch to optimize the NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super model running on the HP ZGX Fury powered by NVIDIA GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip.

Who founded Infinity?
Jeremy Nixon founded Infinity. He is a former Google Brain researcher and co-founder of AGI House, a San Francisco AI community that has launched hundreds of startups.

Is Infinity hiring?
Yes. Infinity recently added Aditya Om (ex-Meta Superintelligence Labs) and Elliot Arledge (CUDA and LLM educator) to its engineering team. Infinity continues to hire Silicon Valley’s top research and inference-library engineers to build the future of recursive self-improvement (RSI). Openings are posted at infinity.inc/careers.
